supporting_observations.claim: The supplied records do not independently establish the alerted dev.sharma RDP session around 13:42 UTC, its source workstation, or its subsequent activity. The available near-time records show a proxy-host DNS lookup for FILE-RB-01 and a FILE-RB-01 HTTPS proxy tunnel, neither of which identifies an RDP session or its user.
At 13:43:29 UTC, PROXY-RB-01 resolved FILE-RB-01.riverbend.local to 10.60.20.20. This establishes name resolution, not remote administration.

At 13:47:09 UTC, FILE-RB-01 made a successful proxy CONNECT to ctldl.windowsupdate.com:443 with a Microsoft-CryptoAPI/10.0 user agent and no identified user. This does not establish whether the alerted session was benign or malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied sensor-coverage metadata, which has no record ID, reports a collection outage from 13:30 through 14:15 UTC for winsec, sysmon, zeek_conn, zeek_dns, and zeek_ssl on FILE-RB-01, WS-DSHARMA-01, WS-CPRICE-01, and DC-RB-01. This encompasses the alerted session start and prevents treating missing authentication, process, and connection records as evidence of inactivity.
Proxy coverage remained available according to the supplied coverage metadata, but the FILE-RB-01 CONNECT records do not identify an RDP source, session, or authenticated user (S22-00080, S22-00228).
claims_not_established: Whether the alerted session originated from the authorized administration workstation WS-DSHARMA-01.
Whether dev.sharma personally initiated and authorized the alerted session.
Whether the session performed approved administration, credential access, persistence, data access, or other malicious actions.
Whether the alerted session was associated with any scheduled change or ticket.
Whether the later lily.okoro RDP-client launch was connected to the alerted session; the launch records identify a different user and later time (S22-00357, S22-00358).
additional_evidence_needed: Obtain the original alert's underlying event, including source IP or hostname, authentication details, session identifier, and detection provenance.

Recover retained local Security and Terminal Services logs from FILE-RB-01 and relevant source workstations for 13:20–14:20 UTC, particularly remote-interactive logons, explicit credential use, session connections, and disconnects.
Recover endpoint process telemetry and independent network or firewall records covering the collection outage to reconstruct the alerted session's source and actions.
Confirm the session with dev.sharma and correlate its actual actions with approved tickets and change records; calendar entries alone are not sufficient authorization evidence.
unrelated_findings: At 14:13:47 UTC, lily.okoro launched mstsc.exe /v:FILE-RB-01 from WS-LOKORO-01, followed by successful target-name resolution (S22-00357–S22-00360). This conflicts with the supplied administration-source policy and warrants a separate review. These records establish client launch and DNS resolution, not a successful RDP login, and do not determine the disposition of the earlier dev.sharma alert.
